extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, creative-writing students, and literary-craft readers
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Hemingway's Iceberg Theory to fiction: create stories whose primary meaning is implied beneath a concrete surface of action and dialogue, relying on the reader to supply the unseen weight. Emphasizes earned omission, spare prose, subtext, and carefully chosen visible details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iceberg Principle (majority of meaning below surface)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The dignity of movement of an iceberg is due to only one-eighth of it being above water." Most of a story's meaning lies beneath the visible surface. The reader feels the unseen mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the visible elements (action, dialogue, gestures) so they implicitly carry much more significance than is explicitly stated; aim for the 'one-eighth' of explicit detail to suggest a larger unseen context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of Knowledge + Omission (earned omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If a writer of prose knows enough of what he is writing about he may omit things that he knows and the reader ... will have a feeling of those things as strongly as though the writer had stated them." Omission only works when the writer fully knows what is omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit because you don't know—only omit details you fully understand. The omission must be earned: the author’s full knowledge of omitted material must inform the surface text so readers can infer it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtext over text
rubrics_metrics.description: What's implied carries more weight than what's said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize implication and beneath-the-surface meaning rather than explicit exposition; let lines of dialogue and small actions suggest larger conflicts or histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust the reader
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave space for readers to infer and participate intellectually/emotionally; resist over-explaining. Use omission strategically to engage reader inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete surface (show observable detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on observable action, dialogue, gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground scenes in tangible, specific behaviors and sensory detail rather than abstract commentary; these concrete details should be the entry points to the unseen material.

rubrics_metrics.name: No explanation of feelings (show, don't tell emotions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the action that produced feelings instead of explaining feelings directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render the causes and manifestations of emotion through behavior and scene detail rather than naming or summarizing emotions for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spare prose (economy of language)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, pared-down sentences and limit modifiers to maintain focus on surface actions that imply deeper meaning; avoid flowery or redundant description that dilutes implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot fragments (in medias res and unresolved endings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start in the middle, end before resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow stories to begin amid action and to stop without neatly resolving everything; fragmentary structure can emphasize the unseen context and empower reader inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol by repetition (suggest rather than declare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use symbol via repetition rather than declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop motifs and repeated concrete images or actions to accumulate symbolic weight instead of overtly announcing meanings or themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: implicit central issue (Hills Like White Elephants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's central issue (abortion) is never named; the reader understands through dialogue and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the example as a model: allow a central conflict or subject to remain unnamed while making it unmistakable through how characters speak and behave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: surface action implies more than it says
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the surface action imply more than it says?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether observable actions and dialogue produce inference of unseen events, relationships, or stakes that outstrip the literal text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: omission is earned by author knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the writer earned the omission by knowing what's omitted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether omissions reflect informed choices (authorial knowledge and craft), not gaps caused by ignorance; omissions should enrich rather than confuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: reader feels the unsaid weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reader feel the unsaid weight?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reader response—does the text produce a felt sense of unseen meaning or emotional depth that motivates reflection or re-reading?

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test: visible details are the right 'one-eighth'
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the visible details the right one-eighth?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the chosen surface details are proportionate and sufficient to suggest the larger unseen context; wrong or extraneous details can mislead or flatten implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Iceberg: hidden emotional response / provoke re-reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader's emotional response should also be partly hidden — story should provoke feelings the reader doesn't immediately understand, prompting return reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design emotional resonance that is ambiguous or not fully articulated on first reading, encouraging readers to revisit the story to unpack feelings and unseen elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related principles cross-reference (defamiliarization, subtext, negative space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections to other aesthetic strategies: Defamiliarization (making the familiar strange), Subtext (Stanislavski), Negative space (visual arts), Suggestion vs. Statement (poetry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these allied techniques to inform implementation of the iceberg approach—e.g., make ordinary things feel fresh, rely on suggestive negative space, and employ subtextual acting/dramatic technique in scenes.
